title: Bangladesh PM to open unity talks with July uprising parties as attacks blamed on Awami League go on
dek: Tarique Rahman's dialogue may start on Monday with the National Citizen Party. Border guards facing West Bengal say they are watching for Awami League activists crossing from India.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Bangladesh's Prime Minister Tarique Rahman is preparing to open talks with the parties that took part in the 2024 uprising against Sheikh Hasina, in an attempt to build a common front against a wave of bombings and arson that police blame on her banned Awami League, according to reports in Dhaka on Sunday.

The dialogue may begin on Monday with the National Citizen Party (NCP), the party formed by student leaders of the July 2024 movement, and is expected to be held at Jamuna, the state guesthouse in Dhaka, according to reports. The NCP's media secretary confirmed the party would be the first to take part, one report said, though others said the agenda had not been finalised and formal invitations had not been sent. Two senior leaders of Mr Rahman's Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) said on Saturday evening that the plan was still being discussed, according to reports.

## Why now

In Parliament on 18 November Mr Rahman described the Awami League as a "terrorist group", called for it to be resisted and urged the "anti-fascist" parties to unite on a single platform, according to reports. The 11-party opposition alliance led by Jamaat-e-Islami held an emergency meeting the next day and welcomed the call. Jamaat's secretary general, Mia Golam Porwar, said unity should rest on implementing the referendum verdict, and the NCP's Akhter Hossen said the party viewed the call for unity "positively", reports said.

The leader of the opposition, Jamaat's Shafiqur Rahman, is abroad and due back on 26 November; the NCP's convener, Nahid Islam, was expected to return from London on Sunday.

The attacks began after Ms Hasina, who has lived in India since August 2024 and was sentenced to death in absentia last year, said she would return to Bangladesh in December. Crude bombs have been set off and vehicles torched across the country, and police stations, Grameen Bank branches and the homes of BNP MPs and leaders have been attacked, according to reports. One count put the toll from 7 to 18 November at 78 crude bomb explosions and 74 vehicles set on fire, with three police installations attacked and 18 police vehicles burned; other counts differ because they use different dates and areas. Police have blamed Awami League leaders and activists.

On Saturday the government sent 90 more platoons of the Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) into districts after arson attacks on Awami League supporters' homes in Narail. About 80 per cent of garment factories in the Gazipur industrial belt had reopened as unrest eased there, according to reports.

## The border with Bengal

The BGB says it has tightened surveillance on all its borders to stop Awami League leaders and activists entering illegally from India. In Jashore, opposite North 24 Parganas and the Petrapole-Benapole crossing, the commander of the 49 BGB battalion told journalists that surveillance had been stepped up at several points, according to reports. In Satkhira, also facing North 24 Parganas, the 17 BGB battalion is installing searchlights and deploying more thermal drones, and its commander said anyone crossing illegally "will be arrested immediately". The moves followed reports that a former Awami League MP had crossed from India and held a secret meeting in his constituency.

## Why it matters for India

Dhaka has repeatedly asked India to hand Ms Hasina over, and Mr Rahman has accused the Awami League of serving "masters" across the border. India has not responded publicly to her plan to return. Tighter BGB patrols on the 2,217 km West Bengal stretch of the border affect crossings, trade at Petrapole and families on both sides, and Bangladesh's visa centres in Kolkata and Siliguri are due to close after 30 November.

## What happens next

The first round of talks with the NCP is expected on Monday, with other July uprising parties to follow. Ms Hasina has not given a date for her return.
